Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x)$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x)$

Moreover, for any even function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ is symmetric across the $y$-axis, so we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=2{\int }_{0}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Notice that $f(x)={x}^{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is an even function. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =(-x)^{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(-x) \\  & =-{x}^{3}(-\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\  & ={x}^{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡x \\  & =f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

So, because $f(x)={x}^{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is an even function, we have

$$
{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}{x}^{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x=2{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{x}^{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$
